--- title: "[StepPolynomial]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Replace numeric columns with their orthogonal polynomial expansion. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/tidymodels/shoez/blob/examples-section/shoez/step_polynomial.py#L333-L533){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python StepPolynomial( columns, *, degree=2, keep_original_cols=False, role="predictor", id=None ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Each selected numeric column ``x`` is replaced by up to ``degree`` orthogonal polynomial columns ``{x}_1``, ``{x}_2``, ..., ``{x}_degree``, or kept alongside them when ``keep_original_cols`` is ``True``. The orthogonal basis is a centering mean plus a QR transform matrix. The effective degree per column is capped at ``n_unique_non_null - 1`` — a column with ``k`` unique values can support at most ``k - 1`` orthogonal polynomial terms. Constant (or all-null) columns get an effective degree of ``0``; `transform()` leaves those columns untouched and emits a `UserWarning`. The caller can chain a zero-variance drop step to clean them up. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [columns]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Selector]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Columns to expand. Accepts a single column name, a list of names, a shoez selector such as ``Selectors.numeric_predictors()`` (see `Selectors` for the full set), or a narwhals or polars selector (``narwhals.selectors.numeric()``, ``polars.selectors.numeric()``). Selectors are resolved against the frame's schema when the recipe is fitted, so the same selector works on any backend. Only numeric columns are meaningful here. [degree]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[2]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum polynomial degree. Must be a positive integer. Default ``2``. Each column's effective degree is the smaller of ``degree`` and ``n_unique_non_null - 1``. [keep_original_cols]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If ``True``, the source columns are kept alongside their polynomial terms instead of being dropped. Default ``False``. [role]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["predictor"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Role assigned to the new polynomial columns. Default ``"predictor"``. [id]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Stable step identifier. Default ``"polynomial"``. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Each selected column is replaced in place by its orthogonal polynomial terms ``{x}_1 ... {x}_degree``: ::: {#e0aeac4a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df = pd.DataFrame({"x": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]}) df ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
x
0 1.0
1 2.0
2 3.0
3 4.0
``` ::: ::: Specifying the step touches no data: ::: {#6b52a7ed .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} recipe = Recipe().add(StepPolynomial(s.numeric_predictors(), degree=2)) recipe ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` Recipe (untrained) Inputs: no roles assigned Steps: step_polynomial(select(role='predictor', type=NumericType)) [untrained] ``` ::: ::: `fit()` learns the orthogonal basis for each column: ::: {#e7d2de2f .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} fitted = recipe.fit(df) fitted ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` Recipe (trained) Inputs: 2 columns — 2 predictors Steps: step_polynomial(x → x_1, x_2) [trained] ``` ::: ::: `transform()` replaces the column with its polynomial terms: ::: {#f4a94e1c .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fitted.transform(df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
x_1 x_2
0 -0.670820 0.5
1 -0.223607 -0.5
2 0.223607 -0.5
3 0.670820 0.5
``` ::: ::: A higher ``degree`` produces more terms: ::: {#f69ef1c7 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} recipe = Recipe().add(StepPolynomial(s.numeric_predictors(), degree=3)) fitted = recipe.fit(df) fitted.transform(df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
x_1 x_2 x_3
0 -0.670820 0.5 -0.223607
1 -0.223607 -0.5 0.670820
2 0.223607 -0.5 -0.670820
3 0.670820 0.5 0.223607
``` ::: ::: ``keep_original_cols`` keeps the source column alongside its terms: ::: {#0a24ba28 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} recipe = Recipe().add( StepPolynomial(s.numeric_predictors(), degree=2, keep_original_cols=True) ) fitted = recipe.fit(df) fitted.transform(df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}
x x_1 x_2
0 1.0 -0.670820 0.5
1 2.0 -0.223607 -0.5
2 3.0 0.223607 -0.5
3 4.0 0.670820 0.5
``` ::: :::
